title: Copy List with Random Pointer
keyIdea: Map every original node to its copy. Walk the list; for next and random, get the copy from the map (creating it on first need), and link the copies. Return the copy of head.

approaches.name: Two passes with a map
approaches.idea: Pass 1: create a copy of every node in the map. Pass 2: copy->next = map[next], copy->random = map[random].
approaches.why: Two walks over the list; the map holds n pairs.

approaches.name: One pass, create copies on demand
approaches.idea: For each node, if next / random has no copy yet, create it; then link this node's copy to them.
approaches.why: One walk; each copy is created exactly once, the first time it is needed.

quiz.q: Why check nodes.find(...) == nodes.end() before new Node?
options: So each original gets exactly one copy; a second copy would break the links

quiz.q: Why can't you just copy next pointers first and random later without a map?
options: random can point to any node, and you need a quick way to find that node's copy

quiz.q: Can the O(n) extra space be avoided?
options: Yes: interleave copies (A → A' → B → B'), set randoms, then split the lists
No, a map is always needed
